messages:
emily_s: Heads-up — JonesCorp reported a big latency + billing spike this morning. They see requests routed to eu-west (higher egress) even though their app is pinned to us-west. Customer opened a support ticket: ~700ms p95 and a sudden 2.3x token billing increase since 04:10 UTC.
sam_nguyen: Ugh. Any recent policy changes? failover config edits?
emily_s: They said product team edited the failover policy via Console at 04:05 UTC. I pulled the audit log: change id `cfg-edit-5421` by rita_kapoor. Screenshot attached in ticket. No explicit rollback yet.
rita_kapoor: That was me — I merged a policy update that consolidated several environment rules. I did a quick QA locally but not full e2e. I pushed a small JSON tweak to the policy array ordering.
matt_lee: Can you paste the exact policy snippet that was deployed? suspect ordering/priority parse.
emily_s: Here is the stored policy blob (from console revision):

```
{
  "failover": ["*", "us-west", "eu-west"],
  "sticky": true,
  "weights": {"us-west": 0.7, "eu-west": 0.3}
}
```

sam_nguyen: There it is. The `"*"` wildcard got promoted to index 0. Runtime treats the priority array as match-first; `*` matches any region and was evaluated before specific entries => immediate fallback to wildcard routing logic which maps to closest available region (our auto-fallback grouped eu endpoints for that account). That explains cross-region hits.
emily_s: Is that a config merge bug (console) or runtime misinterpretation?
matt_lee: A bit of both. Console allowed wildcard at top-level when merging sets; merge function used lexicographic ordering for arrays instead of preserving author-intent order. Runtime then treats the array as precedence. We should never let `*` be earlier than explicit regions.
rita_kapoor: My local file had `"us-west"` first. Merge tool reordered entries when deduping.
sam_nguyen: Repro steps for SRE — I verified with curl against the customer's api-key (redacted):

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-REDACTED" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Response headers show:
```
x-redwood-selected-region: eu-west-1
x-redwood-route-reason: prioritized-wildcard
```

That `prioritized-wildcard` reason is the smoking gun.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0479 — priority: high. Page sent to oncall @sam_nguyen.
sam_nguyen: Mitigation options: 1) revert policy revision in console (fast) 2) hotfix runtime to treat wildcard lower priority than explicit entries (safer long-term). I recommend revert now and schedule runtime fix.
matt_lee: Agreed. I can roll back the revision. Reverting will restore previous array order and stop eu routing.
rita_kapoor: Rolling back now...
rita_kapoor: rollback done — console shows failover: ["us-west","eu-west","*"] at 04:27 UTC.
emily_s: Customer confirms p95 dropped to ~120ms within ~3 minutes and billing spike stopped. They're still asking for post-mortem and prevention plan.
sam_nguyen: Post-mortem items: 1) console merge preserves original array order, never reorder wildcard 2) add pre-commit lint that fails if `"*"` precedes explicit regions 3) add a telemetry alert: if cross-region fraction for a key > 5% and not permitted, auto-notify support 4) runtime change to treat explicit regions as higher precedence than wildcard regardless of array order.
matt_lee: I'll file ENG-8253 and schedule a small runtime patch (non-breaking) to be in next deploy. Also will add a console unit test for merge logic.
rita_kapoor: Sorry team — I should've run the merge locally against staging. Lessons learned.
emily_s: Customer is satisfied with rollback and timeline. They asked for an official RCA and confirmation that we won't silently reorder rules. I'll draft the customer note and postmortem.
oncall-bot: INC-2026-0479 updated: status -> resolved. Assigned to matt_lee for follow-up (ENG-8253).
sam_nguyen: For immediate customer protection: recommend they pin region on the API key or set `allowedRegions` per-key until we ship the runtime safeguard.
emily_s: Noted. I'll add that to the customer reply and include the temporary config snippet for them:

```
{"key_settings": {"allowedRegions": ["us-west"]}}
```

emily_s: Closing thread after postmortem draft. Thanks all :thumbsup:
